steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Fossils are the preserved remains or traces of organisms that lived in the geological past

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Modes of preservation: original material (amber, freezing), replacement (petrification), permineralisation (mineral-filled pores), mould and cast, compression (carbon film)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Trace fossils preserve evidence of activity: footprints, burrows, coprolites, rather than the organism itself

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Body fossils preserve part of the organism: shells, bones, teeth, soft tissues (rare)

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Name five modes of fossil preservation. | Q: What is the difference between a body fossil and a trace fossil? | Q: How can fossils indicate past environments?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: 1) Original material (amber, permafrost). 2) Replacement (original mineral replaced atom by atom). 3) Permineralisation (minerals fill pores). 4) Mould and cast. 5) Compression (carbon film). | A body fossil preserves part of the organism itself (shell, bone, leaf). A trace fossil preserves evidence of the organism's activity (footprint, burrow, coprolite) but not the body. | Living organisms have specific environmental requirements. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Five preservation modes: original, replacement, permineralisation, mould/cast, compression Body fossil = the organism; Trace fossil = the activity Fossils = palaeoenvironment indicators (coral = warm shallow sea, etc.) Fossil record is incomplete: rapid burial and hard parts favour preservation
